anomalies.obs: On the thermocouples sheet (page 5) the MISO output of all three MAX31855KASA parts (pin 7, 'SO') is tied to a global label named 'SO'. On the MCU sheet (page 3) the ESP32-C3 MISO pin (U1 pin 16, GPIO10) carries a global label named 'SD', not 'SO'. Because the two sheets are joined only by global-label names (the root sheet draws no hierarchical ports for this signal), 'SO' and 'SD' are different nets, so the SPI MISO line is broken between the thermocouple interface ICs and the MCU.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the MISO line is a single shared net named 'SO' connected to all three ICs and to the ESP32: 'SO (pin 7, tri-state/MISO) are common nets (SCK, SO) tied to all three ICs and to the ESP32 (U1 GPIO5/SCK, GPIO10/SO).' The MCU-side label should read 'SO' to match the thermocouple-side label.

evidence.quote: thermocouples.kicad_sch (page 5): U2 pin7 'SO', U3 pin7 'SO', U4 pin7 'SO' (global label 'SO')
mcu.kicad_sch (page 3): U1 pin 16 GPIO10 -> global label 'SD'
SCK (pin 5) and SO (pin 7, tri-state/MISO) are common nets (SCK, SO) tied to all three ICs and to the ESP32 (U1 GPIO5/SCK, GPIO10/SO).

anomalies.impact: The shared SPI MISO trace is left floating on the MCU side (the 'SD' net connects to nothing) and disconnected from the three MAX31855 'SO' nets. The ESP32 cannot read any thermocouple word, so all three zones would report a ThermocoupleFault / no valid temperature, and the heater control loop would have no input.

parsed.summary: The board otherwise matches the specification (TPS2121 power mux, AP63203WU buck, TPS1H200 high-side switch, three MAX31855 channels, 5.1k USB-C CC pulldowns, plain-diode D7 on 12V), but the SPI MISO net name is inconsistent across sheets: the thermocouple ICs use global label 'SO' while the ESP32 GPIO10 uses 'SD', breaking the MISO connection and preventing any thermocouple read.
